2B.notes: In a multi-battle sortie, 2B effectively gets 20% damage reduction as long as her shield doesn't fully break. However, healing her is "delayed" by one battle, so her max "HP" is effectively some fraction of her nominal max, depending on how difficult the mob battles are. All it takes is one unlucky battle for her to explode beyond repair. In a single battle, 2B's survivability behaves like normal ships except that she can't be healed by Toolkit or other sources.

A2.notes: Because Berserk procs immediately and lasts for 40 seconds, A2 is slightly stronger in shorter battles, but she is not as biased as the double preloaded torpedo-focused ships like Ibuki and Shimakaze.

Achilles.notes: The Giant Hunter skill description is scuffed. See ALDB for the correct effects.

Admiral Hipper.notes: Hipper's retrofit nearly doubles her DPS by doubling her main gun mounts and adding thick stats. Her unique augment further increases her DPS by ~42% and slightly buffs Hipper class, including Tallinn.

Hipper's retrofit nearly doubles her DPS by doubling her main gun mounts and adding thick stats. Without it, she is pretty useless except for tech. Her unique augment increases her DPS by ~39% and slightly buffs Hipper class, including Tallinn.

Admiral Hipper META.notes: Weak slow, and meh shielding = usually not having +15% dmg.

Adventure Galley.notes: Can +1 ammo, but is weak to planes and uses IX-exclusive guns.

Ajax.notes: The Giant Hunter skill description is scuffed. See ALDB for the correct effects.

Akatsuki.notes: Is bad with or without Hibiki, Ikazuchi, or Inazuma.

Alfredo Oriani.notes: Huge debuff but on special timing.

Amatsukaze.notes: Amatsukaze is quite tanky with poor damage, though her damage is not as bad as Eugen's. She loses around 8% damage if there is no other Sakura Empire ship in the fleet. Her torpedo barrage can freeze enemies for 1 second and slow them for another 0.5 seconds, but that is not useful against bosses as it is difficult to time and is too short in duration.

An Shan.notes: With her retrofit, she becomes one of the highest damage vanguards against light and medium armor in the game currently. She can buff other An Shan class ships and apply a standard Armor Break to enemies. But she is fragile, and her AA is lackluster, making her a mediocre choice for late campaign stages.
Without her retrofit, An Shan is worse than the starter DDs (Laffey, Z23, Javelin).

Anchorage.notes: A very high eHP tank. Her smokescreen also helps to improve the rest of the vanguard's eHP a bit. However, her AA is lackluster.  She lacks any damage buffs for the fleet and her own damage output is mediocre, making her a relatively lackluster choice for single target bosses.

Ardent.notes: Without her retrofit, she doesn't have ARA, so she has nothing going for her.

Ariake.notes: Without her retrofit, she doesn't have ARA, so she has nothing going for her.

Asama.notes: TRP buff. The first CA-specific torp buffer, but better to just debuff the boss with a better ship like Noshiro Muse.

Asashio.notes: Not assumed, but buffs the ships mentioned in the skill.

Astoria.notes: Buffs USS air by not enough for +1 in Offense Buff.

Asuka.notes: On paper, Asuka's numerous barrages and follow-up barrages can let her wipe entire mob waves by herself. And that is true, when the enemy is weak. In Chapter 15 and above, she generally procs follow-up attacks zero or one time per battle. She is also limited by fleet requirements because there needs to be another Senran Kagura ship in the fleet for Asuka to gain 15% EVA and some more minor damage. These ratings assume she is with another Senran Kagura ship for +15% EVA.

Atago.notes: Augment adds about 69% more damage to a bad ship, making Atago decent now. Nice.

Attilio Regolo.notes: Has barrage with every main gun shot, so use a faster gun like Twin 100mm Kai.

Aurora.notes: Aurora offers one of the most powerful debuffs in the game with mediocre/poor stats and everything else. Against enemy DD/CL bosses, Aurora is usually the highest rDPS vanguard ship in the game, even beating Helena's expected 24% main fleet damage. By taking your fleet's hit rate from 70% to 90%, Aurora offers a 29% damage buff. Carriers often have around 70% hit rate against endgame bosses, so Aurora's buff will be a bit less than 29% for vanguard ships and BBs with higher than 70% hit rate. Her low survivability can often be an issue since she needs to live for her debuff to apply. Outside of DD and CL bosses, she is a bad ship.

Avrora.notes: Requires high-DPS vanguard teammates. Has awful stats herself.

Azuma.notes: A tank with decent damage output. However, her AA is mediocre. She also has no damage buffs for the fleet, making her a relatively lackluster choice for single target bosses.

Baltimore.notes: Assumed to be in CV fleet with multiple USS CVs. Augment is decent and now has a small buff for Kearsarge's FP damage.

Baltimore μ.notes: Requires another CV, CVL, or Muse ship.

Bayard.notes: Overall, a really solid vanguard ship, especially for a gold ship. She still has excellent damage output and good eHP. A lot of her damage comes from non-targeted barrages, making her less susceptible to the effects of concealment mechanics in later campaign stages. However, her AA is lackluster.

Belfast.notes: Belfast is good at everything after retrofit. She has very high damage against light and medium armor, strong AA, vanguard smoking and healing, and main fleet damage buff. For single-wave bossing, it's best if there's no other CL in the fleet so that Belfast can buff your main fleet by 6% damage for 3 salvos or airstrikes (on a fast reload pace like 4 salvo META Showdown), but she is still usable with CLs for newer players who need Helena. She also strongly prefers an HE gun, so follow the gear recommendations.
Belfast without retrofit is good at one thing, and that is being either elegant or lewd. She also strongly prefers an HE gun, so follow the gear recommendations.

Black Prince.notes: Assumed to be with an Eagle Union ship, large buff but still bad.

Blücher.notes: Because Blücher redirects a substantial amount of damage to herself, she is best not used as the main tank, but the off tank (rearmost vanguard).

Bogatyr.notes: Robot Companions can block some suicide ships.

Boise META.notes: 2s invincibility for whole vanguard, could be useful for EX if you're bad at dodging. But that means giving up 1 CL FP tech.

Bolzano META.notes: Elite META ship lol. Can tank/AA a little better when solo vanguard, but why would you do that.

Brest.notes: Brest is a very high eHP tank with decent damage output and a small amount of healing. However, her AA is not notable. She also lacks any damage buffs for the fleet, making her a relatively lackluster choice for single target bosses. Brest prefers to use at least one Iris gear for better AA, but for damage, just ignore this Iris gear buff.

Bristol.notes: Bristol's lantern (her main selling point) relies on RNG in vanguard and boss movement. With the speed of a typical vanguard, and with Bristol in the middle, the lantern may have 22% success rate on a boss.

Bristol META.notes: Bristol META's lantern has a 86% chance for a boss to get -10% evasion rate for 10s every 20s, far better than Bristol's lantern due to the double circle and increased size.

Carabiniere META.notes: Carabiniere META effectively applies a permanent armor break with no enemy armor restriction. Don't force a slow torpedo to delay the second skill. Use standard good torpedoes.

Chang Chun.notes: With her retrofit, Chang Chun is one of the highest damage vanguards against light and medium armor in the game currently. She can buff Dragon Empery and Northern Parliament ships and is weaker than her sisters if not doing so. Her eHP and AA are poor, making her a mediocre choice for late campaign stages.
Without her retrofit, Chang Chun is worse than the starter DDs (Laffey, Z23, Javelin).

Chang Feng.notes: Purple and bad. Assumed to be with another Dragon Empery ship.

Chang Wu.notes: If there are 3 Dragon Empery ships in the fleet, Chang Wu gains +60% DPS and a little survivability. Realistically, this would not be a good fleet, so her tiers do not use that fleet assumption.

Chao Ho.notes: With augment, no longer griefs the fleet's AA. Her AA is still bad though. Assume there is another Dragon Empery ship.

Chapayev.notes: As something of a specialist against destroyers, Chapayev decreases the evasion rate of enemy DDs by 10%, which is a significant damage buff for the main fleet and makes her Ark Royal's permanent enemy. She also buffs her own damage against DDs by 20%. Otherwise, though, she’s a pretty middle-of-the-road gold vanguard ship. She has okay damage output, but she is not that tanky, and her AA is lackluster. She does have a potentially powerful damage buff for your vanguards, but proccing it is inconsistent, and the uptime isn't great.

Charles Ausburne.notes: Assumes that beaver badge is equipped on a DD or herself.

Cherbourg.notes: A tank with poor damage output, mediocre AA, and no damage buffs for the fleet, making her a relatively lackluster choice for anything.

Cheshire.notes: Portland with good AA. Better than Eugen's, but still really bad damage.

Chi An.notes: Assumed to be with another Dragon Empery ship.

Chien Wu.notes: Chien Wu is a typical 2024 gold CA with a minor buff for Dragon Empery ships.

Chikuma.notes: Assumed to be with an IJN CV. She buffs CVs. Weak slow. Additional RNG debuff.

Choukai.notes: Yes, this is already updated for her augment.

Clarence K. Bronson.notes: ARA for CV fleet, requires another Eagle Union ship.

Cleopatra.notes: Has fleet air damage reduction but not AA carry-level AA.

Cleveland.notes: Do you like 25% chance per salvo?

Cleveland META.notes: Buffs CLs' FP and AA. Assumed to be with a CL.

Columbia.notes: Augment adds about 15% more damage, including the new weak barrage.

Curlew.notes: Without her retrofit, Curlew doesn't have ARA, so she has nothing going for her.

De Zeven Provinciën.notes: D7P has some of the best AA in the game, decent damage output, and a small amount of healing for the fleet, making her a solid choice for late campaign stages. However, she doesn't have enough eHP to main tank those stages, and her lack of damage buffs for the fleet makes her a relatively mediocre choice for single-target bossing.

Deutschland.notes: Deutschland should be main tank when she has her Unique Augment and not main tank when she doesn't.

Devonshire.notes: A fourth of Devonshire's damage requires that the flagship is a carrier.

Dewey META.notes: Requires a CV or CVL for her double torpedo too.

Dido.notes: Assumes there's another Royal Navy ship for large buffs. Not assuming there is a Queen Elizabeth.

Dmitri Donskoi.notes: Overall, Dmitri is a solid vanguard ship. She has decent damage output and is decently tanky (not enough to consistently main tank late game content). With her fate simulation, you now have some control over which BB her buffs are tied to. For best results, ensure that Götz (as of late 2026) is the BB/BC with the highest FP in your fleet.

Drake.notes: PRake is dead, long live DRake! Drake has very high damage and is decently tanky. Using a flagship who attacks often like Götz further increases her DPS by up to 20%, though that is not assumed by these ratings. However, her AA is lackluster, and she lacks any damage buffs for the fleet.

Duca degli Abruzzi.notes: Large boost from augment brings her close but not close enough to C tier and 2 damage.

Duisburg.notes: Only usable in W14 because her summons can block rammers (but not as well as Momo's flowers). They're fragile though.

Edinburgh.notes: Requires AP gun. Armor break is not up enough to be awarded Offense Buff 1.

Eldridge.notes: With her retrofit, the 20 second cooldown on Operation Rainbow is removed. On top of that, when your flagship fires her main guns or launches an airstrike, she applies a 60% slow to one priority enemy on the screen for 5 seconds. She also has an extra +10 Hedgehog for ASW, and she has decent AA, but her personal DPS is poor. Her biggest weakness is that her invulnerability skill is reliant on RNG to proc. While the activation chance isn't low enough for this to be an issue most of the time, you do sometimes get a run where she just refuses to proc and effectively becomes dead weight. She’s extremely powerful when your vanguard is struggling to live, but when it isn't, she becomes pretty useless. Do not put her in the middle position. Middle is the worst position for Eldridge in PvE, all it does is make her eat torpedoes instead of do the one thing she's meant to do. Note that her retrofit is VERY expensive.

Eldridge has one of the most powerful and unique abilities in the game, which is to make your vanguard invulnerable to damage for 10 seconds at a time. However, without her retrofit, Operation Rainbow starts the battle on a 20 second cooldown, and she doesn't slow bosses. These are significant penalties which grealty limit her potential.

Emden.notes: Buffs KMS FP. Weak slow. Choose between Offense and Defense Buff.

Evertsen.notes: Bad ship and even bad tech!

Fancy.notes: Can +1 ammo, but is weak to planes and uses IX-exclusive guns.

Fargo.notes: Buffs flagship damage but not by enough to be rated. Cargo can draw some enemy fire.

Fei Yuen.notes: Prefers a non-DD Dragon Empery ship.

Felix Schultz.notes: Felix is one of a handful of DDs who want to use a CL gun. She greatly benefits from using a CL gun, and also leans towards AP guns when fighting CL/CA enemies. Follow the gear recommendations, which already blend the relevant DD guns and HE CL guns for you.

Fletcher.notes: Not assumed to be buffing Fletchers.

Fleuret.notes: Buffs Le Hardi class. Do you know who is in Le Hardi class? Me neither. Assumes there is a BB/BC in the fleet.

Forbin.notes: The fleet protection ratings assume the whole vanguard fleet is limited to Iris Libre and Vichya Dominion ships.

Friedrich Carl.notes: Carl's damage contribution is greatly diminished if she is not the main tank. We assume the off-tank ship has decent FP stat for Carl's damage ratings, but you can still use her as a tank with less damage if your off-tank doesn't have high FP.

Fu Shun.notes: With her retrofit, Fu Shun is one of the highest damage vanguard ships against light and medium armor in the game. However, she is very fragile, has lackluster AA, and has no damage buffs for the fleet, making her a mediocre choice for late campaign stages. If you use her retrofit skin, avoid fast-reloading guns like Twin 100mm or Twin 100mm Kai. Her retrofit skin does not have animation time, which means that her weapons can rapid fire without pausing. This greatly increases her main gun DPS relative to other vanguard ships, but if the guns are too fast, then the missiles may get delayed or never fire. So by using the best guns that aren't reloading too fast, Fu Shun cheats to get higher DPS.
Without her retrofit, Fu Shun is worse than the starter DDs (Laffey, Z23, Javelin).

Fubuki.notes: After augment, huge buffs for all DDs. Tiered as a generalist, not a TRP buffer.

Fujinami.notes: Fujinami buffs Sakura Empire DDs. She can use the cheap blue Single 76mm or expensive Single 113mm.

Gallant.notes: The barricades get destroyed so quickly because they're big, so no Defense Buff.

Giosuè Carducci.notes: Bad. Use fast torps. Contradictory skill, requires taking damage while being made of paper.

Gloucester.notes: Gloucester's Out of Ammo buff, like some other damage buffs like Flame's Aggression and Lucky E, is additive with the original Out of Ammo debuff. In the absence of other damage buffs, Gloucester takes your whole fleet from 50% damage to 65% damage, which is a massive 30% increase for the whole battle. So she can be a strong option for getting the third star in campaign if you only use one mob fleet.

Glowworm.notes: Without her retrofit, Glowworm is a very bad ship.
For ramming memes. Use torpedo that reloads between 20 and 23s like quint mags. Mk IX to be tested.

Golden Hind.notes: Can +1 ammo, but is weak to planes and uses IX-exclusive guns. Buffs MOT ships.

Gorizia.notes: Requires Sardegna Empire gear and buffs Zara class or Sardegna vanguard.

Gouden Leeuw.notes: Gouden Leeuw is a tank with extremely high AA, making her an excellent choice for late campaign stages. She has above average damage and a 5% damage buff to HE shells for the fleet. She's an okay choice for single target bossing, but do note that her airstrikes can jam BB salvos.

Grenville META.notes: Buffs DD FP. Buffs FP damage by ~11% for BBs.

Griffin.notes: A 15% EVA buff for the vanguard is worth 6 to 8% survivability. Add another 6% of Griffin's max HP, which is worth less than 6% of vanguard survivability.

Grozny.notes: Augment adds about 32% damage but doesn't take her out of bottom tier.

Guam.notes: Guam is a tank with extremely high AA, making her an excellent choice for late campaign stages. She can also apply consistent armor breaks to bosses (it's a standard armor break but not limited to heavy armor), making her a decent choice for single target bosses though her own damage output isn't anything to write home about.

Guichen.notes: Not assumed, but can do short timeable freezes if with another FFNF/MNF ship.

Hai Chi.notes: Assumed to have another Dragon Empery ship for +12% damage. Smokes.

Hai Tien.notes: Assumed to have another Dragon Empery ship for +12% damage.

Hai Yung.notes: Purple ship from the 19th century, bad.

Halford.notes: Desynced buff. Fs5 gives +40% dmg and very much requires Bearcat (Float) now.

Hammann II.notes: ARA for CV fleet. Free ASW. Flagship Cover. Great skills on a terrible vessel.

Harbin.notes: Harbin has solid damage output and a smokescreen, which improves the rest of the vanguard’s eHP. However, she isn't that tanky, and her AA is lackluster. She also doesn’t have damage buffs for the fleet.

Hardy.notes: Buffs HMS DDs. These ratings already include her unique augment.

Haruka Amami.notes: A one-time timeable debuff. For EX, this comes quite late if she is level 1 without preload.

Hatsuzuki.notes: Assumed to be with 2 other Sakura Empire ships for small FP and RLD buff.

Helena.notes: Helena has one of the most powerful boss debuffs in the game. It's an expected 24% increase in main fleet damage when properly timed and 12% increase in vanguard damage, and this debuff window is worth building single-wave bossing fleets around. However, as newer ships have been introduced with less powerful but more consistent debuffs, Helena's value has gone down for players who value consistency. But none of them are as easily accessible as Helena, so for newer players, she will be a staple in boss fleets for a long time. Helena is not suited for late campaign stages, even campaign bosses, due to her low eHP, unremarkable AA, inconsistency, and inability to help clear waves of enemies that spawn before the boss. Note: Helena should equip SG Radar whenever your main fleet attacks faster than 20 seconds, including but not limited to BBs equipped with ~20 second cooldown main guns and Admiralty Fire Control Table / High Standard Fire Control Radar.

Helena's retrofit gives her some eHP and more flexibility with the timing of her debuff, but it overall isn't a massive improvement. Therefore, she is very suitable for new players to use even without retrofit. Helena has one of the most powerful boss debuffs in the game. It's an expected 24% increase in main fleet damage when properly timed and 12% increase in vanguard damage, and this debuff window is worth building single-wave bossing fleets around. However, as newer ships have been introduced with less powerful but more consistent debuffs, Helena's value has gone down for players who value consistency. But none of them are as easily accessible as Helena, so for newer players, she will be a staple in boss fleets for a long time. Helena is not suited for late campaign stages, even campaign bosses, due to her low eHP, unremarkable AA, inconsistency, and inability to help clear waves of enemies that spawn before the boss.

Helena META.notes: Desynced debuff. Desynced freeze that relies on movement RNG to hit.

Hermione.notes: Assumed to be with another Royal Navy ship for +8% damage.

Hindenburg.notes: Hindenburg is a pure DPS vanguard. She has among the highest damage output for vanguard ships in the game. However, she effectively has no AA, her survivability is relatively low, and she has no damage buffs for the fleet. Compared to newer rainbow vanguard ships who might have lower damage but have buffs for the fleet, Hindenburg's total damage contribution to the fleet is often lower.

Houston II.notes: You've beaten the game. +1 CL FP for you. Oh wait there's Chapter 16.

Ibuki.notes: TRP fleet damager. Very strong preloaded damage, gets relatively weaker as battle length increases.

Isla von Duerer.notes: Slightly benefits from Yumia faction ships, not required. Special armor break with 60% uptime.

Isuzu.notes: Isuzu contributes very little surface damage and requires even more life support to be used in Chapter 15 or higher.
Isuzu contributes very little surface damage and requires life support to be used in Chapter 15 or higher.

Jamaica.notes: Not assumed, but requires and buffs any version of Sheffield.

Janus.notes: Buffs DD/CLs, especially J-class. Assumed to be with 2 other Royal Navy ships, especially a J-class.

Jeanne d'Arc.notes: JdA is effectively Eldridge Retrofit Lite because she significantly buffs the survivability of your vanguard. However, she’s quite mediocre in every other aspect.

Jervis.notes: Jervis buffs Royal Navy DDs if with 2 other Royal Navy ships. Assumed to be in a vanguard fleet of DD/CLs only. Her listed eHP assumes she's being used as the main tank.

Jintsuu META.notes: TRP buff. TRP fleet damager. 3s invincibility with insane burst damage.

John Rodgers.notes: 3% heal for a random ship every 20 seconds is not enough for Rodgers to get a 1 in Main Fleet or Vanguard Protection.

Kaguya Yamai・Yuzuru Yamai.notes: Overall, a really solid vanguard ship. They have excellent damage output and eHP (not enough to consistently main tank late game content). However, their AA is lackluster. Their most noteworthy ability is to temporarily and inconsistently pull stationary bosses close enough to be within the improved range of Oumi’s auxiliary guns.

Kala Ideas.notes: CB with gold rarity. Assumed to not be in a fleet with Item Attacks. And the 3s invincibility is hard to time.

Kasumi (Venus Vacation).notes: Kasumi is like Portland with slightly better survivability, better offense with less reliance on rainbow guns, and 4 gold Bulins and 6k augment exp in debt.

Kawakaze.notes: Uses cheap blue Single 76mm. Or expensive Single 113mm. Buffs IJN DD damage against cruisers.

Kawakaze META.notes: Requires blood shadows to stay alive to exceed Plymouth in DPS. If they die fast, still better than normal Kawakaze.

Kazagumo.notes: A somewhat mediocre ship on first impression, Kazagumo sees a lot of use because she’s one of the least terrible ships with the Air Raid Assistance skill. She’s also a Sakura Empire ship, so she can help proc Shinano’s buffs for IJN CVs. She only exists to buff the damage of your CVs against single target bosses and is being powercrept in this role slowly but surely. On the bright side, she is much more easily obtainable than her alternatives.

Kent.notes: HEY Shikikan! Do you like 25% chance per salvo?

Kirov META.notes: One-time 15% debuff. Desynced slows. Great for EX if you left her at level 1 for some reason.

Kitakaze.notes: Ignore the skill about counting torpedo hits. Do not favor Quintuple Magnetics over equal-rarity Quadruple Magnetics.

Kizu.notes: Prefers more Sakura Empire vanguard ships in the fleet. These ratings assume there is one other, for two total. Kizu has worse damage and survivability than Nayoro.

Kronshtadt.notes: Kronshtadt is a very high eHP tank with decent damage output. She lacks any damage buffs for the fleet, making her a relatively lackluster choice for single target bosses.

Kurumi Tokisaki.notes: Kurumi is the budget (but limited) version of Laffey II. She fulfills a very similar role, being an almost unkillable cockroach. She does this by generating clones and switching to a clone when she sinks, and she can generate clones faster when there are more enemies on screen. These clones can also inconsistently body-block suicide boats from reaching the main fleet. Furthermore, her Time-Eating Castle zones can slow down or stop submarines and suicide boats. These skills make her an extremely good tank for campaign stages, though her AA and ASW aren’t as good as Laffey II's.

Köln.notes: Chooses from 10 possible barrages. More ASW if she equips the Fl 282 Kolibri helicopter.

Köln META.notes: Köln META's timed 10% EVA debuff is not enough to reach a +1 in Offense Buff. She improves your fleet's ASW if she equips the Fl 282 Kolibri helicopter, but this is not recommended due to her poor survivability. Contrary to what the EN skill text says, she does NOT increase your submarines' damage by 20%. Instead, she increases your ships' damage dealt to enemy submarines by 20%.

Königsberg META.notes: Königsberg META buffs vanguard RLD by 15% and damage by about 5%, not significant enough for Offense Buff rating.

L'Audacieux.notes: Buffs DDs, especially FFNF/MNF DDs. Assumes there is another FFNF/MNF ship. Worse in short battles.

L'Intrépide.notes: No better than the baseline unretrofitted, unaugmented starter DDs, L'Intrépide should be avoided by new players.

Laffey II.notes: The cockroach of Azur Lane, Laffey II is among the tankiest ships in the game in a very unique way, to the point where she can main tank Chapters 15 and 16 while running two ASW auxiliaries. If Laffey II sinks, you are probably doing something wrong. Her AA is also above average, making her an excellent ship for late campaign stages. However, her own damage is lackluster, and she lacks any significant damage buff or debuff for the fleet, so she’s not an ideal choice single-target bosses.

Lala Satalin Deviluke.notes: Discount black hole on AoA, and minor air buff.

Le Hardi.notes: Le Hardi has a bonus if the main tank is an Iris Orthodoxy ship, but that is very restrictive, and putting her as main tank is ill-advised.

Le Mars.notes: Assumes the vanguard fleet is limited to Iris Libre and Vichya Dominion.

Le Triomphant.notes: When Le Triomphant is the main tank, she does more damage at the cost of worse AA. But please do not use her as main tank. Dead ships don't do damage.

Le Téméraire μ.notes: Both barrages have two torpedoes with ~40% geometric hit rate, so Le Téméraire μ heals the main fleet for an insignificant amount and heals ~9% of one vanguard ship.

Leipzig.notes: Buffs cruisers and reduces ramming damage.

Lenja.notes: Prefers mobbing for sinking low HPs. Prefers Heavenly Armillary aux. These ratings assume that there is another Yumia collab ship generating Environmental Mana.

Lila Decyrus.notes: Assumes there is another Atelier ship to generate enough AP for her.

Little Anchorage.notes: How dare I say she's a bad ship

Little Cheshire.notes: Requires life support to be used in Chapter 15.

Little Ägir.notes: 15% slow that is somewhat but inconsistently timeable due to CB gun angles.

London.notes: Without her retrofit, London still buffs vanguard FP, but she lacks the "cannon" part of "glass cannon".

Lyme.notes: Can +1 ammo, but is weak to planes and uses IX-exclusive guns.

Magdeburg.notes: Mob ship only. Augment improves damage by 29%, but she's still bad.

Marie Rose.notes: Marie Rose's skills mean that she is stronger in shorter battles. Her large torpedo damage buff expires after 3 torpedo salvos, which takes about 40 seconds, and her other buffs expire after 60 seconds.

Matchless.notes: TRP buff. 61% chance for a Quint Torp, assuming 100% hit rate. Needs at least LB2, level 30.

Maury.notes: RNG for survival. Higher speed is usually not a good thing.

Memphis META.notes: Weak slow. Defense buff for some META ships.

Miller.notes: Miller needs to be main tank for some minor buffs, but she has very bad tankiness, so you just have to give up those buffs. All she has Carrier Escort, which doesn't even proc immediately.

Misaki.notes: Buffs DOA ships and prefers another DOA ship.

Mogador.notes: The horniest ship in the game. She has high overall damage output and buffs torpedo damage (including torpedo bombers) by 6%. She has a desynced and very short freeze which can be synced with for one rotation at best in practice, making its value rather dubious. Her AA is nothing special, and her eHP is relatively low, so she's not a brilliant choice for late campaign stages.

Momo Belia Deviluke.notes: Momo's flowers block ramming ships (both normal Bombing Ships and the fat Kagerou Productions) extremely consistently. She must use her unique augment to spawn a second flower. She also has two delayed 25% slows after her "All Out Assault". Can use Plymouth gun or Single 150mm.

Monica.notes: To buff fleet torpedo and AA, Monica needs 5 enemy airplanes to die in the AA range. Only 1/4 of her 15s barrage applies the 10% damage taken debuff. So each time, the barrage has an approximately 44% chance to apply that debuff.

Moskva.notes: One of the strongest overall vanguards in the game, she combines really high eHP with some of the best vanguard damage in the game. She also buffs the fleet AA circle’s range by 5, which is very useful for the fleet’s AA and the consistency of shooting down planes, though her own AA is lackluster. Moskva can also be paired with Nakhimov to activate the latter's freeze.

Musketeer.notes: Needs a long time to ramp up her damage.

Naganami.notes: TRP buff and torpedo damage dealer for battles under 20 seconds.

Nana Astar Deviluke.notes: Uses cheap blue Single 76mm or expensive Single 113mm. Great mob damage but whiffs against moving bosses.

Napoli.notes: Napoli is one of the tankiest vanguard currently in the game, and she has decent damage output. However, her AA is lackluster. She also lacks any damage buffs for the fleet, making her an unimpressive choice for single target bossing.

Nayoro.notes: Much of Nayoro's damage comes from her timed skill barrage, making her a reasonable choice for new players without good gear. She can replace Laffey/Javelin/Z23.

Neptune (Neptunia).notes: Assumes there is another Neptunia ship.

Nicholas.notes: How many RNG skills can you fit on a ship?

Ning Hai.notes: Yat Sen with Ning Hai or Ping Hai, known as the Great Wall of China, is extremely tanky but has poor damage output and bad AA and ASW. It's a niche pairing that is seldom used. When not sortied with Yat Sen, Ning Hai and Ping Hai are very bad.

Yat Sen with Ning Hai or Ping Hai, known as the Great Wall of China, is extremely tanky but has poor damage output and bad AA and ASW. It's a niche pairing that is seldom used. When not sortied with Yat Sen, Ning Hai and Ping Hai are very bad.

Northampton II.notes: Assumed to be in a CV fleet with a USS CV flagship.

Noshiro.notes: TRP buff. TRP defense works against bombing ships.

Noshiro μ.notes: TRP buff. Works with submarines too. Note that Oxytorps are Sakura Empire gear. If playing manual torpedoes, the faction gear requirement will be satisfied by Oxytorp.

Nürnberg META.notes: There needs to be enemy airplanes so that Nürnberg META doesn't lose ~11% eHP.

Ognevoy.notes: Tiny heal. Don't expect her to chain barrages against high-level enemies.

Orage.notes: Orage has flashy torpedo barrages but no relevant fleet buffs or AA.

Otto von Alvensleben.notes: Most vanguard ships who can choose between destroyer and light cruiser guns in the same slot should use destroyer guns due to pure DPS or reload time for All Out Assault procs. For Otto, the penalty of longer reload times of CL guns is effectively waived by her AoA count requirement.

Ozornoy.notes: Assumes there's another NP ship. Depending on your device, you might get 2 or 3 barrages per proc, a 10% DPS difference.

Pamiat' Merkuria META.notes: Weak 20% slow. Contrary to what the game claims, it is 27.5 range, not 55 range. So the slow is also inconsistent with about 40% chance.

Ping Hai.notes: Yat Sen with Ning Hai or Ping Hai, known as the Great Wall of China, is extremely tanky but has poor damage output and bad AA and ASW. It's a niche pairing that is seldom used. When not sortied with Yat Sen, Ning Hai and Ping Hai are very bad.

Yat Sen with Ning Hai or Ping Hai, known as the Great Wall of China, is extremely tanky but has poor damage output and bad AA and ASW. It's a niche pairing that is seldom used. When not sortied with Yat Sen, Ning Hai and Ping Hai are very bad.

Pittsburgh.notes: Consistent armor break for BBs. Ideally flagship fires first.

Plymouth.notes: Plymouth has excellent damage output, decent survivability (enough to main tank some but not all endgame content), and an 18% damage buff to your flagship if she's a battleship. Her AA is lackluster, however.

Pola.notes: Assumed to be with another Sardegna Empire ship. Buffs Sardegna Empire vanguard, especially Zara class.

Portland.notes: Portland is a stat-stick, and her skills are not worth leveling up. Taking Defense Order from level 1 to level 10 increases your vanguard survivability by 1%. Do not use Indianapolis.
Portland is a stat-stick, and her skills are not worth leveling up. Taking Defense Order from level 1 to level 10 increases your vanguard survivability by 1%. Do not use Indianapolis.

Portsmouth Adventure.notes: Can +1 ammo, but is weak to planes and uses IX-exclusive guns.

Princess Hime.notes: She carries not-so-big cargo. Buffs SSSS (the collab faction) ships.

Prinz Adalbert.notes: Was a decent gold-level tank for 2022.

Prinz Eugen.notes: Eugen is an all-around mediocre gold heavy cruiser. This wall has good eHP but is terrible in every other aspect. You get her from login in rewards, and you can use her if you really desire, but it is not recommended.

Prinz Eugen μ.notes: Buffs vanguard damage. Assumes there is a muse ship for a small damage buff.

Prinz Heinrich.notes: Was a decent gold-level tank for 2021-2022, and a mediocre unique augment in 2025 didn't fix her.

Prinz Moritz.notes: Yes, follow the gear recommendations. Yes, purple Triple 283mm is better than all rainbow CA guns for Moritz. Yes, she with a purple gun matches the performance of shiny Azuma with shiny gun.

Prototype Bulin MKII.notes: This "ship" is strictly used as limit break fodder for gold ships. DO NOT use her for combat outside of the one mission that requires it. Bulins are really weak.

Regensburg.notes: Assumes there is another Iron Blood ship. Desynced buff for Iron Blood.

Reisalin Stout.notes: Can ignore buffs for Atelier ships. Stronger in shorter battles. 40s damage is 3/3/2, 80s damage is 2/2/1. Grand Bomb MUST be in Slot 2 (the usual torpedo slot), and Laute Plajig MUST be in Slot 3 (the usual AA slot). Do not put them in any other slot! They do not need to be enhanced to improve the weapons, but enhancing gear does give stats.

Reno.notes: Reno reduces damage taken by carriers by 10% for four battles, so this doesn't benefit the more dangerous out-of-ammo battles. Assume that there is at least one carrier in the fleet for her damage ratings. For Light Damage, assume the enemy is DD or CL and there are one or two allied carriers.

Rikka Takarada.notes: Uses special gear. Battle Tracto Max, Buster Borr, and Sky Vitter should be enhanced to +10 and MUST be equipped in the correct slots for their respective special weapons. There is another improvement at +13, but do mind your gold plate usage, and the gain from +10 to +13 is less than for normal weapons. If with Yume Minami and Chise Asukagawa, the special fusion Gridman is good for dumping damage in short battles.

Ritsuko Akizuki.notes: Buffs Idolmaster ships or other ships with her equipped cargo.

Roon.notes: Augment is huge, avg +30% FP over 80s, barrage, +5% dmg, about 10%/10%/30% main gun mod multiplicative increase.

Roon μ.notes: Desynced freeze and debuff relies on movement RNG to hit.

Royal James.notes: Can +1 ammo, but is weak to planes and uses IX-exclusive guns.

Ryu Lion.notes: Ryu Lion has decent damage output and is decently tanky (not enough to consistently main tank late game content). However, her AA is lackluster, so she does need to be supplemented by ships with good AA in plane-heavy late campaign stages.

Saint Louis.notes: Saint Louis requires an HE gun. Her augment is huge, giving +15% main gun, an ok barrage, another +10% all dmg, and another +15% to light/medium damage.

San Diego.notes: San Diego has some of the best AA in the game. That, combined with decent damage output and eHP, makes her an excellent ship for late campaign stages. However, her own damage is lackluster, and she lacks buffs for the fleet, so she’s not an ideal choice for single-target bosses. Her augment barrage is bugged and will probably never be fixed, but her damage is serviceable. Her retrofit is VERY expensive, and she needs her Unique Augment on top of it. If you're new, just craft her unique augment and skip the retrofit until you get to Chapter 12.

Without her retrofit (but with her Unique Augment), San Diego has decent damage and fantastic AA. However, her retrofit is a significant upgrade to her capabilities. Rush for the Modernization node by skipping the bottom row. The bottom row costs 8 gold retrofit blueprints and is low priority until Chapter 13.

San Francisco.notes: Read her skills. The ratings do not all apply simultaneously, choose between tanking, healing, and damage.

Santa Fe.notes: Decent DPS, and Flares are nichely huge debuff but on special timing.

Scylla.notes: Time her torpedoes with carrier airstrikes.

Seattle.notes: Seattle has a 15% damage reduction when sortied in the off tank (right most slot) position, and this is not reflected in her listed eHP.

Sendai.notes: Without her retrofit, Sendai doesn't have her flares, so there's very little reason to use her.
Huge debuff but on special timing. Also TRP buff for DD/CL.

Shandy.notes: Shandy offers various buffs for the vanguard, where each effect is active 4/15 of the time on each ship in expectation. They are worth about 8% damage increase and 4% survivability for the vanguard.

Shigure.notes: Depending on whether she's with Yukikaze, Shigure can opt for fleet protection or increasing her poor damage to slightly-better-than-poor damage.

Shimakaze.notes: Something of a one-trick pony, Shimakaze has excellent (but not top-tier) damage against heavy armor enemies and 2 preloaded torpedo salvos, which are very useful for clearing the first mob wave in a fight. In every other aspect, she’s rather mediocre; she’s fairly fragile, her AA is bad, and she doesn’t have damage buffs for the fleet. If you want 2 preloaded torpedoes salvos for clearing trash mobs quickly, Ibuki is better at it and cheaper to invest in.

Shimanto.notes: Shimanto is a very good ship for late campaign stages because she has excellent AA, a small amount of healing/shielding for the vanguard, decent damage output, the ability to extinguish fires on your main fleet ships, and decent eHP. However, her lack of damage buffs for the fleet makes her unimpressive for single-target bossing.

Shiranui.notes: For battles that Shiranui with her unique augment (probably has to be maxed, but we don't know) participates in, a tech pack (does it have to be T3 or T4?) in the rewards can very rarely be replaced by a special T3 Sakura Tech Pack (Display Sample). It's basically a trophy sitting in your depot. Many details are unknown since the drop rate is so low and the logic is all server-side.

Shiratsuyu.notes: TRP buff. Even with Retrofit + Augment, she doesn't meet the thresholds for the second lowest tier.

Shropshire.notes: Without her retrofit she lacks the "cannon" part of "glass cannon".

Sirius.notes: A somewhat mediocre ship on first impression, Sirius sees a decent amount of use because she’s one of the relatively few ships with generic buffs for carriers, and said buffs are quite strong against DD, CL, or CA bosses. She only exists to buff the damage of your CVs. Otherwise, she has bad damage output, she’s fragile, and she has lackluster AA. Fortunately, her buffs persist for the whole battle even if she sinks.

Specialized Bulin Custom MKIII.notes: This "ship" is strictly used as limit break fodder for rainbow ships. DO NOT use her for combat. Bulins are really weak.

Superb.notes: Superb's personal damage scales very greatly with the flagship's reload speed. When with a flagship who reloads in 18 seconds, Superb is a generic non-tank vanguard ship who has decent AA. Or, by being paired with a flagship who reloads in 7 seconds like Götz rather than 18 seconds, Superb's DPS increases by a massive 50% to reach the high end of all vanguard ships.

Surrey.notes: Surrey is another Portland with AA. Unlike Cheshire, Surrey actually does damage, but she has slightly worse AA.

Suzunami.notes: Timeable slow on torpedo hit is weaker than Aegir's, but Suzunami has much higher hit chance.

Suzuya.notes: Although Suzuya gains a massive 75% RLD and 15% FP buff after hitting enemies enough times, it is not significant enough to change the relative ranking of recommended guns just to reach the max stacks a few seconds earlier. Therefore, the recommendations are standard, without considering CL vs CA gun reload or shell count.

Swiftsure.notes: Around 50% uptime on a decent debuff. Use a gun with high shells per second, like 6 shells in 3 seconds.

Tai Yuan.notes: With her retrofit, Tai Yuan is one of the highest damage vanguard ships against light and medium armor. She provides some shields for the vanguard but is fragile and has lackluster AA, making her a mediocre choice for late campaign stages.
Without her retrofit, Tai Yuan is worse than the starter DDs (Laffey, Z23, Javelin).

Takahashi.notes: Takahashi is a very good ship for late campaign stages because she has excellent AA buff and good AA, a small amount of shielding for the vanguard, good damage output, and decent eHP. However, her only damage buff for the fleet is a 40% slow that is not synced to typical main fleets, making her unimpressive for single-target bossing. When there is more than one enemy, Takahashi gets a roughly 10% damage bonus.

Tallinn.notes: Tallinn's unique augment adds damage and changes her slight preference for an Iron Blood or Northern Parliament main gun to a requirement.

Tanikaze.notes: Without her retrofit, Tanikaze lacks her torpedo debuff, so there's no reason to use her.

TRP buff. More inconsistent and worse than Noshiro μ. Assuming you manual a quintuple torpedo such as Mk IX, and assuming the torpedoes have 100% hit rate, there is a 61% chance to apply the torpedo debuff. For EX high scoring, she needs to be at least LB2, level 55 to unlock her skill.

Tashkent.notes: Buffs SN DDs and has a weak slow. Not assumed, but could pair with Nakhimov.

Tiger.notes: Tiger, the not-so-glass glass cannon. Hindenburg too weak? No problem, give her 20% more DPS, 15% more tankiness, and strong AA.

Tohka Yatogami.notes: Tokha has excellent damage output, good eHP, and 10% damage reduction for the flagship. Her AA is lackluster, however, so she does need to be supplemented by ships with good AA in late plane-heavy content.

Trafalgar.notes: Trafalgar is one of the best universal debuffers in the game if your flagship has main guns. Her 10% evasion rate debuff is almost unrivaled for consistently increasing the damage your fleet deals against bosses. Although there are greater debuffs like Helena's or Aurora's, they are not as consistent or universally applicable as Trafalgar's. She also applies 15% slow effectively permanently. She's a decent option for late campaign stages thanks to her good AA and decent personal damage, though do note she has relatively low eHP for a rainbow DD.

Trieste.notes: Huge debuff but on special timing.

Trinidad.notes: Pretty good dps actually, a third of it being from the 15s barrage. But just below the threshold for a 2.

Tsukushi.notes: Tsukushi relies on a very powerful barrage every 20 seconds to do damage. Her augment is extremely strong despite being bugged negatively in the first version. She gets a small bonus for being with up to two other Venus Vacation ships, so these ratings assume there is one other ship.

Ugolino Vivaldi.notes: Assumed there are 3 Sardegna Empire ships.

Universal Bulin.notes: This "ship" is strictly used as limit breaking fodder for gray, blue, or purple ships. DO NOT use her for combat outside of the one mission that requires it. Bulins are really weak.

Unzen.notes: Unzen is a pure DPS vanguard. She has among the highest damage output for vanguards in the game. She has poor AA, her eHP is relatively low, and she has no damage buffs for the fleet. Compared to newer rainbow vanguards which might have lower damage output but buffs for the fleet, Unzen's total damage contribution to the fleet is often lower.

Unzen-chan.notes: Like her mom, Unzen-chan has double preloaded torpedoes and parallel torpedo reloading. However, Unzen-chan's torpedoes do much less damage, and she also has significantly less survivability. One torpedo salvo from Ibuki beats two from Unzen-chan.

Vicksburg.notes: Vicksburg has decent AA, but really all she does is semi-high damage by virtue of having 2 MGM plus DD secondaries.

Vittorio Cuniberti.notes: Cuniberti's fate simulation solidly increases her damage and survivability. She now has high DPS and middling survivability. Use fast torps as shown in the recommended gear.

Voroshilov.notes: Tankiness requires enemy planes. Weak slow and small FP buff. Explicitly say that she's not assumed to be with Nakhi.

Watarase.notes: Assumes there is a Sakura Empire flagship with under 20s reload (4 in 80s). Damage depends on the reload time of the flagship.

Wichita META.notes: Pure GLASS cannon who can pull crazy numbers if the stars align to keep her alive long enough at low HP.

William D. Porter.notes: An interesting ship, to say the least. Willy D has excellent AA, a skill that reduces the damage taken by your flagship, and a universal 5% damage debuff that is effectively permanent. Additionally, when she fires her torpedoes, she buffs the damage of your flagship and Eagle Union ships by 10% for 10 seconds. However, compared to other rainbow DDs, her damage output is noticeably lower, and her survivability can vary depending on what torpedoes you equip her with and where you're using her.  Large chunks of her survivability are conditional; she relies on a 15% damage reduction triggered when the fleet is shooting at planes, along with an 8% self-heal after she fires her torpedoes. Consequently, if she isn't in an environment with high plane density—or if she's equipped with slower-reloading torpedoes to sync her buffs—she becomes noticeably squishier, potentially becoming a liability.

Yat Sen.notes: With her retrofit, Yat Sen's requirements are relaxed, so she only needs to be paired with another Dragon Empery ship. While her AA is slightly above average, her damage output is mediocre, and she lacks significant damage buffs for the fleet.

Yat Sen is one of the tankiest vanguard ships in the game with the caveat that she is sortied with another Dragon Empery ship. While her AA is slightly above average, her damage output is mediocre, and she lacks significant damage buffs for the fleet. When sortied with just another Dragon Empery ship, she’s fairly mediocre. However, when sortied with Ping Hai and/or Ning Hai, she buffs their eHP significantly, forming the Great Wall of China. This pairing is fairly niche, however, as all 3 have bad damage output, mediocre AA, and no damage buffs for the main fleet.
Yat Sen is one of the tankiest vanguard ships in the game but only if she's sortied with Ping Hai and Ning Hai. Her damage output and AA are both mediocre.

Ying Swei.notes: With augment, no longer griefs the fleet's AA. Her ASW is still bad though. Assume there is another Dragon Empery ship.

Yukino.notes: Yukino offers various buffs: 10% zombie heal twice, armor break every 15 seconds, 8% damage for a main fleet ship twice, and a torpedo buff not worth mentioning. These ratings assume that vanguard ships are the first to go below 20% HP and be healed.

Yuubari.notes: Augment: smoke, shield, and shit ton of barrages.

Yuudachi.notes: A decent all-around vanguard, she has decent damage overall. However, she isn't that tanky, her AA is bad, and she lacks any damage buffs for the fleet. Despite what her background might lead you to believe, she’s closer in performance to 2026 gold vanguards than 2026 rainbow vanguards.
Without her retrofit, Yuudachi is one of the worst gold DDs.

Yuudachi META.notes: A decent all-around vanguard ship, Yuudachi META has solid damage output. However, she isn't that tanky, her AA is bad, and she lacks any damage buffs for the fleet.

Yuugure.notes: Without her retrofit, Yuugure doesn't even have ARA, so she has nothing going for her.

Z1.notes: Assumed to be buffing a full Z fleet.

Z14.notes: Z14 improves the main tank's survivability by ~15% when Z14 is not the main tank.

Z28.notes: Requires and buffs Z class. Smokes.

Z35.notes: Augment adds a very strong mine (effectively a delayed bomb), increasing her damage by about 70%.

Z47.notes: Uses cheap blue Single 76mm. Or expensive Single 113mm.

Z52.notes: Jack of all trades, master of none pretty much sums up Z52. She has good personal damage, good AA, and the Flagship Cover skill (-25% damage received by your flagship). She’s pretty tanky and can main tank a decent amount of endgame content. On top of all of that, she has a 5% universal damage debuff that lasts for 10 seconds when your upper main fleet ship launches an attack. Because she can do just about everything with no weaknesses, she's incredibly versatile for just about any fleet.

Zara.notes: Very minor buff for Zara class.

Ägir.notes: A very high eHP tank with decent damage output. She can apply a standard armor break and apply a 60% slow with her torps. However, the latter is difficult to make use of due to the difficulty of syncing the torpedoes for multiple salvos / airstrikes. They also need to hit the boss in order to apply the slow, and she doesn't have very high HIT stat. Her AA is also lackluster.

Émile Bertin.notes: Requires sortieing with DDs. Buffs FFNF or MNF DDs.
Prefers to sortie with DDs. Buffs FFNF or MNF DDs.
